items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: Steve Dunn, the other trumpet player and I got along well together and worked out some nice duos on certain numbers.

ctx.x: The first night I played with Broadus was for a dance in Dayton, Ohio. Broadus and his musicians had come to Cincinnati early that morning and as I was not ready to leave with them, he told me that I could come to Dayton later by train. Dayton is about 50 miles from Cincinnati. Broadus travelled by car as did most of the orchestra then and today.

Broadus played C-melody sax and the alto player was Henry Jamerson who was known as "Speechless" because he was not a great talker. I had seen Jamerson in the orchestra of Lloyd Scott when they had played at Elmwood Town Hall. Steve Dunn was a trumpet player with a very nice style and Slaughter Campbell was a banjo player as good as Bob Robinson. I can't remember who the pianist was but the drummer was and the tuba player was a big fellow who weighed 240 pounds. He could just get a double B tuba around his body…

Broadus had a big second-hand Packard and the tuba player sat in the back on the left side which made the car sag in a manner that seeing the car from the back it looked as though it was going to turn over. We left Dayton after the dance and headed for Lexington and my place in the car was in the middle in the back seat next to the tuba playen and slept almost as comfortable as if I was in bed.
